title: Effects of vitamin D supplementation on FGF23: a randomized-controlled trial
authors: Trummer C, Schwetz V, Pandis M, Grübler MR, Verheyen N, Gaksch M, et al.
population: Adults with arterial hypertension and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D below 30 ng/mL in the Styrian Vitamin D Hypertension Trial, Graz, Austria; post hoc analysis
funder: The Styrian Vitamin D Hypertension Trial was supported by funding from the Austrian National Bank (Jubilaeumsfond projects 13878 and 13905); open access funding by the Medical University of Graz. No statement on the role of the funder was found.
inKindSupport: Fresenius Kabi provided the study medication (Oleovit D3); BIOMEDICA Medizinprodukte supplied FGF23 assay kits; BioPersMed (publicly funded COMET K-project) provided analysis equipment.
authorConflicts: The authors declare that they have no conflict of interest.
result: Vitamin D3 2800 IU/day against placebo for 8 weeks raised 25-hydroxyvitamin D by 11.1 ng/mL (95% CI 8.9 to 13.3). Effect on C-terminal FGF23 in the whole cohort: 0.374 pmol/L (-0.024 to 0.772), P=0.065. In subgroups with baseline 25-hydroxyvitamin D below 20 ng/mL (n=70) and below 16 ng/mL (n=40), FGF23 rose by 0.973 pmol/L (reported 95% CI -0.032 to 1.979, P=0.019) and 0.593 pmol/L (0.076 to 1.109, P=0.022).
